title: The Ophan's demand: build plan
eyebrow: Design area: the demand loop · step 2 of 2 · nothing built

short.lead: This turns your answers into five build steps. The first lands what's already made: the Wick and the Ophan's art. The next three build the tuning file and 5-minute raids, the Ophan's arrival, and the demand itself, which replaces the coin debt. The last is a playtest, solo and then with two players, before anything else gets built. Most of the work is already filed as issue #418 (the Ophan arrives and catches players) and issue #419 (the artifact quota replaces the debt), so the plan updates those rather than starting over. Five choices are open, and every one has room for your own answer.
short.hint: Tap a step for what it does and what it needs. Under Changes is the list of what the debt code keeps, changes or drops.
items: check
Exists
What is already built or filed
done
The Wick (#417, the Lantern Warden turns into the Wick) is finished on the branch AjsAgent/fear-wick, with tests and a co-op check, but no pull request is open yet.
The Ophan's model, its five clips and the import rules are in pull request #414, not yet checked in Unity.
Issue #418 (the Ophan arrives in hunted raids and catches players) and issue #419 (the Ophan's artifact quota replaces the debt and the Collector) are filed and match most of your answers.
A raid lasts 600 s today (ExtractionZone.RaidDurationSeconds). The portal bell rings at 120, 60 and 30 s left (MusicDirector).
The coin debt and the Collector live in 8 runtime files and 11 test files (listed under Changes).
Nothing from you.
lock
Step 1
Land what is already made
you
I open the Wick's pull request into staging-2026-10-11.
You merge #414 (the Wick and the Ophan's art), the Wick's pull request, and #422 (the Lair pile that keeps its place), so every later step starts from one base.
Your merges. Merging can't be undone cleanly, so it stays your call.
hammer
Step 2
The tuning file and 5-minute raids
OphanDemandTuning, one data asset holding every number from the questions page, with DemandsToConfront dropped.
The raid's length is read from RaidSeconds (300) instead of the 600 s set on ExtractionZone.
A test checks that every default loads and that no value is out of range.
Nothing from you.
eye
Step 3
The Ophan arrives and catches (#418, updated)
On a raid where a demand is due or owed, the Ophan arrives HuntWindowSeconds (60) before the portal closes, passes through walls and hunts.
Caught holding the piece: it takes the piece and leaves at once, and everyone is safe. Caught empty-handed: you die.
It reuses the Wick's kill and the guard-turned event, and is tested on both machines in a co-op check.
Your answer to choice 2: how its coming is announced.
loop
Step 4
The demand replaces the debt (#419, updated)
Before the first raid, the ledger shows the first demand: a sketch of a piece deep in the vault, at least FirstPieceMinRoomsFromPortal (6) rooms in. It is due at the end of that raid.
After that, a demand falls due every 3 to 5 raids. Placing the piece in the Lair, or being caught holding it, pays it.
While a demand is owed, every raid is a hunt and its haul is taken.
The piece has a faint mark within 6 m for the first 3 demands.
The coin debt and the Collector go, per the list under Changes.
Your answer to choice 3, on the debt code.
search
Step 5
A solo playtest, then a two-player one
you
First you play the first raid and three more alone. Solo has to be fun on its own, not just survivable.
Then you play the same again with two players, on your two PCs with your two Steam accounts.
Both runs are timed against the 5-minute checklist you answered in the comparison thread.

What feels wrong is fixed by changing numbers in the tuning file. If solo is too hard or too easy compared with two players, the fix is a setting that scales with how many players are present, added only if the test shows it's needed.
Upgrading isn't designed or built until both runs have been played.
You alone, then you on both PCs. About 20 minutes each.
hand
Unity
Who runs Unity
you
Steps 2 to 4 need Unity to compile and run the tests and the co-op checks. This cloud container has no Unity, so those checks have to run on a machine that does.
Your answer to choice 4.

LairHubManager: the debt

The company owes coin, paid when the Collector calls.
The company owes the Ophan a piece.
The save slot instead keeps the current demand: which piece, and how many raids are left. Old saves with a debt still load, and the debt is ignored.

CollectorRules.cs and the Collector's events
Dropped: the shares, the take and the Collector's line.
The Collector takes each wizard's share at setting out.
Nothing collects coin; coin only buys things.
Also drops the Collector's two events in LairEvents.cs. CollectorTests.cs and the debt parts of CoopRulesTests.cs are replaced by tests for the demand.

RaidDirector: the call at setting out
The Collector's call and the debt's growth at setting out go; the replicated debt becomes the replicated demand.
Setting out: the Collector calls, then the debt grows by 50; clients get the host's debt.
Setting out: the demand's raid count steps down; clients get the host's demand.
The host still owns the campaign state and replicates it to clients, as it does today (RaidDirector, the host-campaign sync).

RaidHudPresenter and MainMenuScreen

Coin still comes from selling and is kept per wizard. With the debt gone it has nothing to buy until the upgrading area is designed and built.

OphanDemandTuning
The one data file for every demand number.

RaidSeconds 300, HuntWindowSeconds 60, FirstDemandDueAfterRaids 1, RaidsBetweenDemandsMin 3 and Max 5, HuntEveryRaidWhileOwed on, SpoilsTakenWhileOwed 1.0, ExtraPiecesPerMissedDemand 0, UnscheduledVisitChance 0, HuntSecondsAfterPaid 0, PieceMarkRadius 6 m, PieceMarkLastsForDemands 3, FirstPieceMinRoomsFromPortal 6.
The numbers are scattered or don't exist yet.
One asset, edited in the Inspector.
A playtest that feels wrong is fixed by changing a number.
